detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Some vLLM args are derived from verl's own config (TP, DP, expert parallelism, LoRA, routing replay) but could also be passed through `rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm`. Which source won depended on where verl wrote the derived value, and neither direction was reported: `tensor_parallel_size` from `engine_kwargs` replaced verl's, while `enable_expert_parallel` was always overwritten with `expert_parallel_size > 1`. With the default `expert_parallel_size=1`, an explicit `engine_kwargs.vllm.enable_expert_parallel=True` became `False`; every GPU then held all experts (and their LoRA buffers) and vLLM reported no memory for the KV cache.

This PR keeps verl's config as the only knob for these args. `engine_kwargs` naming one of them now fails at server start with the config to set instead:

| vLLM arg | set instead |
|---|---|
| `tensor_parallel_size` | `rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size` |
| `data_parallel_size` | `rollout.data_parallel_size` |
| `enable_expert_parallel` | `rollout.expert_parallel_size` (= TP × DP) |
| `enable_lora`, `max_lora_rank` | `actor_rollout_ref.model.lora` |
| `enable_return_routed_experts` | `rollout.enable_rollout_routing_replay` |

The check replaces the delta_sharded-only TP/DP override checks. The one in-repo script that set `enable_expert_parallel` next to `expert_parallel_size` drops the redundant line, and the perf doc names the rollout config.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+enable_expert_parallel
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

- `TestEngineKwargsManagedArgs` in `tests/workers/rollout/test_vllm_cli_args_on_cpu.py`: managed args (including the hyphen spelling) raise with the right config name; other args pass through.
- Ran the module in a vLLM container: 33 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [x] Update the documentation (perf best practices).
- [x] Add unit test(s).

**Compare equivalent JSON arguments before rejecting them.**

When PD disaggregation supplies `kv_transfer_config`, the launch path puts `json.dumps(self._disaggregation_kv_transfer_config)` in `derived`. If engine kwargs contain the same configuration as a dictionary, this comparison raises `ValueError`. Both values would produce the same CLI JSON through `build_cli_args_from_config`. Normalize JSON-valued arguments before comparing them.

+def merge_derived_engine_args(
+    args: dict[str, Any], engine_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any], derived: Mapping[str, Any]
+) -> None:
+    """Write the engine args verl derives from its own config into ``args``.
+
+    ``rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm`` passes through the vLLM args verl does not manage. An
+    arg verl derives (parallel layout, LoRA, routing replay, ...) has a single source,
+    verl's config: repeating it in engine_kwargs with the same value is accepted, a
+    different value raises instead of being silently overwritten.
+    """
+    given = {key.replace("-", "_"): value for key, value in engine_kwargs.items()}
+    conflicts = [
+        f"{key}={given[key]!r} (verl derives {value!r}; set "
+        f"{_DERIVED_ENGINE_ARG_SOURCES.get(key, 'the rollout config that controls it')} instead)"
+        for key, value in derived.items()
+        if key in given and given[key] != value

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Preserve an explicit expert-parallel request when the size is 1.**

With `expert_parallel_size=1` and `engine_kwargs.vllm.enable_expert_parallel=True`, this line derives `False`. `merge_derived_engine_args` then raises `ValueError`, so the server cannot launch. This rejects the configuration that the PR intends to preserve. Use the requested value when the size is 1, and retain the conflict check for an explicit `False` when the size is greater than 1. Update the `ep-flag-without-ep-size` test, which currently expects this rejection. vLLM supports enabling expert parallelism explicitly. Security architecture risk: 🔵 Low · up to bf520
The change rejects contradictory launch settings before starting the affected inference engine. No introduced security vulnerability was established. Risk is bounded to launch compatibility and incomplete cleanup assurance when distributed startup fails. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.

Its direct effect is acceptance or rejection of startup settings for the configured rollout deployment; broader tenant or environment exposure is not established. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The new gate prevents conflicting passthrough values from silently replacing selected VERL-owned launch settings. It does not add authentication, restrict who can supply rollout configuration, or validate every available engine option. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — Server actors reserve ports before merge validation and remain referenced by the launch owner after a method failure unless another owner tears them down.
